lines.text: “I am in prison, but the outside world is just a larger prison.”

blocks.text: Group Monologue takes many individual voices and weaves them into one powerful performance. It’s the perfect follow-up to Writing in Role.

items.text: Students take about a minute to look over their Writing in Role piece and pick the one sentence or phrase they feel is most powerful.
If students already have numbers from Roll Call, use those! If not, quickly give each student a number.
In order, one after another, each student reads their chosen line aloud.

blocks.text: For example: after writing as Wangari Maathai in prison, a student chooses the following line to share:
“I am in prison, but the outside world is just a larger prison.”
Heard alongside everyone else’s lines, each phrase adds a new layer to Wangari’s story.
Line by line, a single monologue takes shape, built from the whole class’s voices.

Every student contributes, and every voice matters. The result is a celebration of the class’s shared thinking, often surprisingly moving, with a real sense of togetherness. Students only share one line they’ve chosen themselves, so it still feels safe.
